input.task: What does the SECOND 'Add to cart' link say?

provenance: PR #60 R10, and the reason ADR-032 exists. The two-pass name tier introduced in round 1 was two SETS, and `index` was applied to each in turn — so when the exact pass held fewer than `index + 1` matches the loop fell through and indexed the FOLDED set instead. On `case-twins.html` that made `index: 0` and `index: 1` return the same element and answered "what does the SECOND link say?" with the first link, where base `6b016b5` raised a loud `element-not-found`. ADR-032 settles the semantics rather than patching the symptom: a tier is ONE match set, chosen once — the folded pass is a fallback for an EMPTY exact pass, never a supplement to a non-empty one — and every downstream rule (`near`, `index`, `many`, uniqueness, ambiguity) reads that one set. Union was the other candidate and is rejected in the ADR: unioning puts the case twins back into the set `index` indexes, which is exactly the round-1 defect (R1) returning by another route.

triage.note: This is the case that makes the byte-for-byte claim TRUE rather than nearly true: with one set per tier, a page carrying an exact-case match never consults the fold at all, so `index` counts what it counted before T-M42-20 — here, one match, and a second index is a loud failure. The four sentences that claimed this while it was false are corrected in the same commit (resolver.py, SKILL.md, tasks/TODO.md, and the index case's own provenance).
